subject: CodexAI POC — SDK auth, routing & request/response clarifications
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: CodexAI POC — SDK auth, routing & req/resp clarifications

Hi Samuel —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap + a short list of follow-up items so we can scope the POC and internal owners. Thanks for walking us through the demo.

Top-line ask: confirm architecture choices for SDK auth, routing, and request/response semantics so we can produce a first-cut integration doc and code snippets for your engineers.

Notes / clarifying topics (please reply inline where you can):
- SDK & auth: will you want a browser-based integration or server-only? We generally recommend short-lived guest tokens (issued by your backend) for any client-side SDK usage; production service keys should never be embedded in a client. We can provide an auth proxy example.
- Routing / model variants: do you need fixed model pinning for determinism or are cost-latency fallbacks acceptable (e.g., primary = tele-8k, fallback = tele-3b) when capacity constrained?
- Structured output & tool/function calling: will you rely on Redwood's function-calling JSON schema, or do you prefer a post-processing layer? If you want function calling, share the exact action schema and we can validate expected tokens.
- Embeddings & rerankers: are you planning to use a single embedding model for both retrieval and reranking, or separate models? We typically batch embeddings (size 32–128) and run a lightweight learned/ML reranker only for top-K.
- Request/response schema specifics (chat vs completions + tokenization): we need to lock down behavior for:
  * max_tokens semantics (generation cap vs token budget across messages)
  * stop sequence behavior with streaming responses
  * streaming semantics for UI (delta messages vs final JSON payloads)

Attachments: PoC mutual action plan (codexai-poc-mup.pdf) and placeholder SDK snippets doc.

Can you respond with the items you want covered in the POC (auth pattern, routing policy, expected QPS, success criteria)? Ben and Karthik will pick up the engineering notes once we have that.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap. Quick answers/high-priority clarifications from our side below.

High level: we want a responsive in-product assistant embedded in our web app (browser + backend). SLOs: page-level response < 300ms for the first token, conversational throughput ~40 req/s for a single pod.

Questions we need clarified before the POC kickoff:
1) Auth: we prefer a short-lived token flow. Can your SDK support a signed, expiring guest token (15 min) issued by our backend? We plan to rotate keys via KMS. Also: can Redwood support mTLS for the internal service-to-service channel?

2) Chat vs completions: our UX needs structured JSON intent outputs. When should we use chat models vs completion endpoints for stable JSON outputs? Are chat models with function-calling strictly better for schema enforcement?

3) Tokenization & max_tokens: we saw different behavior across models. We need explicit guidance: is max_tokens a hard cap on generated tokens after the prompt or a soft cap combined with prompt tokens? Also, we sometimes send long context (system + history) — how does Redwood calculate billing and enforcement?

4) Stop sequences + streaming: if we stream tokens, how is a stop sequence handled mid-stream? Will the stream close immediately when a stop pattern is detected, and will the final chunk include an explicit indication that stop triggered? We need deterministic client-side handling.

5) Embeddings/reranker flow: for retrieval + rerank, does Redwood recommend running embeddings on the same model family as the reranker? Should we expect significant latency if we do on-demand reranking for top-50 vs a batched offline rerank?

6) Example SDK snippet for browser + server exchange and how to call streaming vs non-streaming endpoints (prefer minimal example with scoping for auth).

If you can answer 1–4 briefly and provide a small snippet for 6, we can lock scheduling. We'd like to aim for a short technical call with your infra engineer next week (prefer UTC mornings).

—Samuel
Samuel Park
Head of Integrations, CodexAI
samuel@codexai.com

Samuel — thanks for the clear list. Looping Karthik and Ben; Karthik will draft a short tech note + example snippets. I answered the high-level parts below; Karthik, feel free to expand and add concrete code.

Quick answers from Redwood (high-level):
- Auth: yes, we support short-lived guest tokens (15m–1h) issued by your backend. Pattern: your backend holds a long-lived service key in KMS -> call Redwood token issue endpoint to mint a scoped token -> exchange to browser. We also support mTLS for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted customers can use IP allowlists + KMS.

- Chat vs completions & structured output: use chat models with function/tool calling when you need strict JSON shape and deterministic fields. Completions can work for free-form templates but function-calling gives better extraction and structured validation on the server side.

- max_tokens semantics: Redwood enforces max_tokens as a hard cap on generated tokens (post-prompt). Billing counts prompt tokens + generated tokens. If you have prompt-heavy contexts, use prefix truncation / KV cache to reduce repeat cost.

- Stop sequences + streaming: streaming will emit token deltas as they are generated. Redwood detects stop sequences server-side; when stop condition triggers the stream sends a final chunk with an explicit metadata frame {"stop_reason": "stop_sequence"} (or equivalent in the SDK event). Client should handle that explicit termination event.

- Embeddings/reranker: recommendation is to use a single embedding family for retrieval and an ML reranker for top-K (e.g., embed-1 -> vector store -> rerank-1). On-demand rerank for top-50 will add latency; batch/async rerank or learned lightweight rerank is better for production.

Karthik — can you add a tiny code snippet showing: 1) backend minting guest token, 2) browser connecting to Redwood streaming endpoint, 3) handling stop event and final payload? Please attach to the shared Drive and we will push to their team.

Marissa

- Billing: prompt + generation tokens. We can provide tokenization tooling to estimate costs before the test.
